message.content:
**Signatories of the United States Declaration of Independence (July 4, 1776)**  

| State | Signers (in order of appearance on the original parchment) |
|-------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| **Delaware** | George Read, Caesar Rodney, George Calvert |
| **Pennsylvania** | Robert Morris, Benjamin Rush, George Clymer, James Smith, George Taylor, James Wilson, George Ross, John Morton, George Washington (as President of the Continental Congress), John Penn |
| **New Jersey** | William Franklin, John Witherspoon, Francis Hopkinson, John Hart, Abraham Clark, William Livingston, John Hart, William Livingston |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott |
| **Massachusetts** | John Hancock, Samuel Adams, John Adams, Joseph Warren, Paul Revere, John Hancock (again as President of the Congress), John Hancock (again as President of the Congress) |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll (again) |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, James McClenahan |
| **New Hampshire** | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| **Virginia** | Richard Henry Lee, Francis Lightfoot Lee, Carter Braxton, George Wythe, Thomas Jefferson, James Madison, George Mason, Edmund Randolph, Thomas Jefferson (again) |
| **New York** | William Floyd, Philip Livingston, Lewis Morris, Robert R. Livingston, John Jay, William Floyd (again) |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, Roger Williams |

> **Total:** 56 signers.

These men represented the thirteen colonies and signed the Declaration on August 2, 1776 (the date the parchment was signed). The document was adopted by the Continental Congress on July 4, 1776, but the signatures were added later. The most famous among them include **Thomas Jefferson** (author), **John Adams**, **Benjamin Franklin**, **John Hancock** (who famously signed with a large, bold hand), and **George Washington** (who served as President of the Congress at the time).
